title: Book Three · Chapter 29: The Yellow Flowers
story:
On Sunday, Dad comes home after his morning at Mr Sun's place.

Mum has put the last finished coat inside a clean bag. Its owner collected the other one yesterday.

Ronan is ready by the door. Mum looks at his shoes.

“Lunch first.”

“I'm ready for that too.”

They eat rice and vegetables. Dad asks about the market. Ronan tells him about the rings and the wrong lid.

“Did you buy the rings?”

“No. Kai bought the tin.”

“A useful morning.”

“And nuts.”

“A very useful morning.”

After lunch, they leave the dishes clean and go out. Mum carries her green and grey bag. Dad puts his hands deep in his coat pockets.

They take the road toward the river. The path beside the water is busy with families. Ronan stays beside his parents and watches a bird hop along the wall.

Mum stops at a stall of flowers.

There are red flowers, white ones, and a small bucket of yellow ones. She touches one yellow petal with a finger.

“These,” she says.

The woman at the stall asks how many.

Mum chooses a small bunch. She pays and carries it above her bag, away from the rough cloth.

Dad looks at the yellow flowers.

“For the table?”

“For me. On the table.”

He smiles. “That works.”

They walk on. At a low wall, Dad stops to rest. Ronan stands beside him. Mum studies the flowers and turns the bunch around.

The sun comes out between two clouds. The yellow looks brighter.

“You can put them by your chair,” Ronan says.

“Then I will see them while I work.”

Dad shifts a little on the wall. “Can I see them too?”

“From your chair.”

They stay until the sun goes behind the clouds again. Then they take the longer road home past the quiet shops.

At one window, Dad stops to look at a wooden cabinet. He likes the smooth corners. He points out a small shelf inside. Mum waits with the flowers. Ronan looks at the little round handles.

No one goes inside. After a minute, Dad turns away, and they keep walking.

At home, Mum washes an old glass jar. Ronan brings water from the kitchen. Dad puts a plate under the jar to protect the table.

The flowers lean to one side at first. Mum cuts a little from two stems and arranges them again.

Ronan moves his school papers away. There is still room for the flowers and three cups.

Mum sits down beside them.

“Tea?” Dad asks.

She nods. “This time, you make it.”

He goes into the kitchen. Ronan puts his chair on the other side of the table, where he can see the flowers too.

## 词句提示

petal＝花瓣；bunch＝一束；cabinet＝柜子；stem＝花茎。

## 理解问题

1. 父母怎样兑现周日外出的安排？Mum为谁挑了黄色花？
2. 回家后，一家三人分别怎样安置这束花？

## 读句子

**Dad puts a plate under the jar to protect the table.**

拆开看：Dad / puts a plate under the jar / to protect the table.

Dad／在玻璃罐下面放一只盘子／用来保护桌面。
